source.title: ResiDual Transformer Alignment with Spectral Decomposition
source.authors: Lorenzo Basile; Valentino Maiorca; Luca Bortolussi; E. Rodolà; Francesco Locatello

page_placements.theme: Attention heads: monosemantic vs polysemantic roles

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports experiments on vision-transformer attention heads, but does not test any listed version about neuron poles, neuron explanation accuracy, or neuron-based attribution graphs.
record.gate_note: The paper measures attention-head geometry, specialization, and cross-dataset similarity. These are related to unit specialization but are not measurements of the neuron-pole claims. Zero-shot classification and ResiDual results do not measure the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study analyses attention-head representations (PCA, intrinsic dimension, text decomposition, cross-dataset spectral similarity) in vision transformers and proposes ResiDual for zero-shot alignment. It does not measure neuron poles, the share of single-job neurons, the InceptionV1 cat-car neuron, neuron-based attribution graphs, or held-out activation prediction of neuron explanations. Head specialization is a related but different unit (attention heads, not neurons), so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that vision-transformer heads are low-dimensional and grow more nonlinear with depth. Specialization, where present, is traced to a few principal components and is stable across datasets. Reweighting task-aligned head principal components (ResiDual) approaches fine-tuning-level zero-shot accuracy with few parameters.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes vision-transformer attention heads with PCA, text-based decomposition, and cross-dataset comparisons; it does not audit language-model neuron poles or score neuron explanations on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that head similarity declines with model depth and that the first principal component captures head semantics in some cases but not others.

fits_no_version.finding: In OpenCLIP-L late-layer heads, the first principal component sometimes reproduces whole-head TextSpan descriptions (L22.H8, Z=4.93) and sometimes does not (L20.H8, Z=0.02).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Vision-transformer attention-head roles are sometimes concentrated in one principal component and sometimes distributed across several.

fits_no_version.finding: Head similarity between ImageNet and other datasets follows a consistent dataset ordering across encoders (mean correlation 0.97). Similarity drops with depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Specialized roles of vision-transformer attention heads are stable across data distributions and consistent across encoders.

fits_no_version.finding: MLP units in OpenCLIP-L have much higher linear dimensionality than heads, and the authors describe their text decompositions as showing strong superposition of concepts (Figure 11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In vision transformers, whole MLP-layer outputs are less interpretable and more mixed than attention-head outputs.

record.problems: The experiments concern vision-transformer attention heads rather than language-model neurons. Textual descriptions and cross-dataset similarity do not establish that an explanation predicts activations on held-out examples.
record.rows_left_out: Zero-shot classification, head-selection, and ResiDual performance results were left out because they do not measure neuron interpretation or any listed claim version.

rows.subject: OpenCLIP-L
rows.operation_detail: Compared head-representation PCA bases between ImageNet and other datasets using the proposed spectral cosine similarity.
rows.measure: Cross-model Pearson correlation of dataset similarities, averaged over heads
rows.value: mean correlation coefficient 0.97 across different encoders
rows.note: The result concerns similarity profiles of vision-head representations across datasets and models, not neuron-pole job counts.
rows.check: Cross-model correlation of dataset-similarity profiles for heads; the 0.97 is across encoders, not specific to OpenCLIP-L as subject. Not a neuron-interpretability measure.

rows.subject: OpenCLIP-L
rows.operation_detail: Compared descriptions selected by TextSpan on whole head representations with OMP on each head's first principal component.
rows.measure: Absolute Z-score agreement between selected description sets
rows.note: The paper describes this as high agreement and shows similar letter-related descriptions. It is a comparison of description-selection methods, not a test of explanations on held-out activations.
rows.check: Agreement between two description-selection methods for one head; a method comparison, not a measure of neuron job count or explanation accuracy.
